questions.prompt: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
questions.note: Au comes from aurum, the Latin word for gold.

questions.prompt: Which part of a cell is often called its powerhouse?
questions.note: Mitochondria release energy from food.

questions.prompt: What is the pH of pure water at room temperature?
questions.note: Below 7 is acidic and above 7 is alkaline.

questions.prompt: Which gas makes up most of Earth's atmosphere?
questions.note: Nitrogen is about 78 per cent of the air.

questions.prompt: Which blood cells carry oxygen around the body?
questions.note: They contain haemoglobin, which is what makes blood red.

questions.prompt: Light travels at about how many kilometres per second? (Give it to the nearest thousand.)
questions.note: Light takes about eight minutes to reach us from the Sun.

questions.prompt: Which is the smallest bone in the human body?
questions.note: It sits inside your ear and is only about three millimetres long.

questions.prompt: A tomato is botanically a fruit.
questions.note: It grows from a flower and holds the seeds.

questions.prompt: Which scientist is best known for the theory of evolution by natural selection?
questions.note: His book On the Origin of Species came out in 1859.

questions.prompt: What is the chemical formula for water?
questions.note: Two hydrogen atoms join one oxygen atom.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Canada?
questions.note: Ottawa is on the border between Ontario and Quebec.

questions.prompt: Which river flows through Cairo?
questions.note: Almost all Egyptians live near the Nile.

questions.prompt: Which is the smallest country in the world by area?
questions.note: It is entirely inside the city of Rome.

questions.prompt: Which sea lies between southern Europe and North Africa?
questions.note: Its name means middle of the land.

questions.prompt: Mount Kilimanjaro is in which country?
questions.note: It is the highest mountain in Africa.

questions.prompt: The ancient rock-cut city of Petra is in which country?
questions.note: Petra is known as the Rose City for the colour of its stone.

questions.prompt: Which line of latitude is at zero degrees?
questions.note: North of it is the Northern Hemisphere and south is the Southern.

questions.prompt: Greenland is the largest island in the world.
questions.note: Australia is bigger but counts as a continent.

questions.prompt: Which desert covers much of southern Mongolia and northern China?
questions.note: Many dinosaur fossils have been found in the Gobi.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Japan?
questions.note: Tokyo is one of the biggest cities in the world.

questions.prompt: In which year did the Berlin Wall come down?
questions.note: Germany became one country again in 1990.

questions.prompt: Who was the first Roman emperor?
questions.note: Augustus was Julius Caesar's great-nephew and adopted son.

questions.prompt: Which ancient people built Machu Picchu in the Andes?
questions.note: It sits high in the mountains of Peru.

questions.prompt: In which year was Magna Carta sealed in England?
questions.note: It limited the power of King John.

questions.prompt: Which explorer sailed across the Atlantic in 1492 on a voyage that reached the Americas?
questions.note: He thought he had reached Asia.

questions.prompt: In which year did the Second World War end?
questions.note: The war in Europe ended in May and in Asia in September.

questions.prompt: Who is credited with inventing the telephone in the 1870s?
questions.note: Bell was born in Edinburgh.

questions.prompt: Johannes Gutenberg is famous for introducing which invention to Europe?
options: The printing press with movable type
questions.answer: The printing press with movable type
questions.note: It helped books become cheaper and more common.

questions.prompt: Who was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize?
questions.note: She won in 1903, and won a second Nobel Prize in 1911.

questions.prompt: The Byzantine Empire was ruled from which city?
questions.note: Today it is called Istanbul.

questions.prompt: What does the abbreviation CPU stand for?
questions.note: The CPU is often called the brain of a computer.

questions.prompt: What is the square root of 144?
questions.note: 12 times 12 is 144.

questions.prompt: What is the value of pi, to two decimal places?
questions.note: Pi is the distance round a circle divided by the distance across it.

questions.prompt: Which of these numbers is a prime number?
questions.note: A prime has exactly two factors, itself and one.

questions.prompt: How many bits make up a byte?
questions.note: A byte can store one letter of text.

questions.prompt: Who proposed the World Wide Web in 1989?
questions.note: He worked at the CERN laboratory.

questions.prompt: How many degrees are there in a right angle?
questions.note: A full turn is 360 degrees.

questions.prompt: Which language has the most native speakers in the world?
questions.note: English has more learners in total, but fewer native speakers.

questions.prompt: How many letters are in the English alphabet?
questions.note: Five of them are vowels: a, e, i, o and u.

questions.prompt: What was the programming language Python named after?
questions.note: It was named after Monty Python's Flying Circus.

questions.prompt: How many players from one team are on court at a time in basketball?
questions.note: Basketball was invented in 1891 in the USA.

questions.prompt: Which city hosted the 2012 Summer Olympic Games?
questions.note: London was the first city to host the Games three times.

questions.prompt: Who painted The Starry Night?
questions.note: He painted it in 1889 while staying in a hospital in France.

questions.prompt: In which Shakespeare play does the character Prospero appear?
questions.note: Prospero is a magician living on an island.

questions.prompt: How many keys does a standard piano have?
questions.note: That is 52 white keys and 36 black keys.

questions.prompt: Origami is the traditional paper-folding art of which country?
questions.note: The word means folding paper.

questions.prompt: Who wrote The Hobbit?
questions.note: It was first published in 1937.

questions.prompt: Who invented the Rubik's Cube?
questions.note: He was a Hungarian professor of architecture.

questions.prompt: Every how many years is the men's FIFA World Cup normally held?
questions.note: The first tournament was in 1930 in Uruguay.

questions.prompt: In which city were the first modern Olympic Games held in 1896?
questions.note: They were held in a restored ancient stadium.
